memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They mounted the onyx stones in gold filigree settings and engraved them like a seal with the names of the sons of Israel. Then they fastened them on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel, as the Lord commanded Moses." - Exod 39:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two onyx stones, engraved with the names of Israel's tribes, mounted on the high priest's shoulders.

Every time Aaron entered God's presence, he carried those names with him. The people were not left outside hoping he would remember them. Their names went in on his shoulders.

That is one of the clearest pictures of intercession in the Old Testament, and it points straight to Christ. He is able to save completely those who come to God through Him, because He always lives to intercede for them (Heb 7:25). Right now, He is praying for His people.

Notice the word "memorial." The stones were a permanent reminder before God. Not a request made once and then forgotten, but a standing presence.

And notice they were engraved "like a seal" — cut into the stone, permanent, not painted on to fade.

Your name is not lightly written. Isaiah says God has engraved us on the palms of His hands (Isa 49:16). Jesus bears the marks of the nails still.

If you feel forgotten today — overlooked, unheard, one of billions — remember the shoulder stones. God's people go into His presence by name.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you believe Christ is praying for you right now?
2. Whose names are you carrying into God's presence?
3. What does it mean to you that your name is engraved rather than written in pencil?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You that You carry my name before the Father. Teach me to carry others in prayer as You carry me. Amen.
